Application Materials.content:
While filling in your application, you will be required to submit the following:
- Updated Resume
- 2 Personal Statements
- Contact details of two referees. For shortlisted candidates, 2 reference letters may be required.
- Copy of NRIC/FIN/Passport (in PDF or JPEG format)
- Softcopies of relevant certificates and academic transcripts
Personal Statement Questions:
1. Explain in **500-600 words** your career and personal aspirations, and your motivation for pursuing the Master of Sustainability.
2. Discuss in **500-600 words** one of the following topics: i) describe your greatest weakness and how you have tried to overcome it; or ii) describe your outstanding talents, skills and inherent abilities that are not reflected in your academic qualifications and records; or iii) describe the situation with the greatest ethical complexity that you have faced in your professional or academic life, and how your input helped resolved it.
Please complete the application form accordingly and attach copies of the documents as instructed. Your application will only be processed when all the documents have been received. Verification of original documents is required upon matriculation into the programme; failing to do so may result in applicants having to withdraw from the programme.

Interview Requirements.content:
- For shortlisted candidates, **2 reference letters and an interview will be required**.
- Shortlisted candidates would be invited for an interview.
- Admission interviews will be conducted for short-listed candidates.
- FAQ: “Are there admission interviews? Yes. We will contact you for an admission interview after receiving your online application.”
- The programme states that it takes into consideration the candidate’s interest, aptitude, GMAT/GRE scores, recommendation from referees, previous academic achievements and **admission interview performance** when doing the assessment.

Application Deadlines.content:
The Programme accepts applications on a rolling basis. Applications should be submitted no later than **30 June** for the intake starting in **August** of the same year.
| **APPLICATION DEADLINE** | |
| --- | --- |
| Final | **30 June 2026** |

Academic Requirements.content:
- **Good undergraduate degree**.
- Applicants from **all degrees** and those looking to transit into sustainability related roles are encouraged to apply.
- No prior work experience is required; work experience is not mandatory.
- Applicants whose first degree is not related to Sustainability may apply if they have a keen interest in sustainability and ESG.
- Undergraduate CGPA may be used in place of GMAT/GRE/SMU Admission Test scores for: **SMU Bachelor’s degree graduates with a minimum cGPA of 3.4/4.0 (within 5 years of graduation)**; **SUTD/NUS/NTU/SUSS/SIT Bachelor’s degree graduates with a minimum cGPA of 3.6/5.0 (within 5 years of graduation)**. Meeting the cGPA academic criteria does not guarantee admission.

GRE GMAT Requirements.content:
- Pre-requisites include a **good score in SMU Admissions Test or GMAT/GRE**.
- For MST admission, **EITHER the SMU Admissions Test OR GMAT (Graduate Management Admission Test) / GRE (Graduate Record Examinations General Test) is mandatory**. Applicants who do not have a GMAT/GRE Score are strongly encouraged to attempt the SMU Admissions Test.
- If applicants have not taken the GMAT or GRE, they are encouraged to take the SMU Admission Test. Alternatively, they may first submit the online application and arrange for the GMAT/GRE test to be taken as soon as possible, including the test date.
- Undergraduate CGPA may be used in place of GMAT/GRE/SMU Admission Test scores for: **SMU Bachelor’s degree graduates with a minimum cGPA of 3.4/4.0 (within 5 years of graduation)**; **SUTD/NUS/NTU/SUSS/SIT Bachelor’s degree graduates with a minimum cGPA of 3.6/5.0 (within 5 years of graduation)**. Meeting the cGPA academic criteria does not guarantee admission and candidates may still be recommended to submit GMAT/GRE/SMU Admission Test scores.
- Official Score Reports can be sent via the following Institution Codes: **GMAT: F8D-02-56**; **GRE: 2861 (Department Code: 4102)**.
- A GMAT/GRE test score is required for all candidates; alternatively, applicants may choose to take the SMU Admission Test in lieu of GMAT/GRE as entry criteria to the MST programme. In some cases, depending on overall credentials, the MST Admissions Team may still advise candidates to take the GMAT/GRE test to improve chances for admissions offer.
- All MST applicants are eligible to take the SMU Admission Test in lieu of GMAT/GRE as entry criteria to the MST programme. The **SMU Admissions Test score cut off is an overall score of 55**. Each applicant is only allowed a maximum of **3 test attempts per intake (including deferment)**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
- A valid TOEFL/IELTS score is required if the medium of instruction of your undergraduate studies was not in English.
- IELTS, UKVI (Academic) or TOEFL is required for applicants whose Degree programme (Bachelor's/Master's/PhD) was not taught in English. Minimum Requirements [IELTS/UKVI (Academic)/TOEFL]: **IELTS/UKVI (Academic) - Min 6.5**, or **TOEFL - Min 90**.
- Students who did not attempt their undergraduate studies in English are required to attempt the IELTS (International English Language Testing System) and TOEFL (Test of English as a Foreign Language). It must be taken within the last **two years** at the time of submitting your application.
- For all the abovementioned tests, you may first email the unofficial score to the Admissions Team while requesting for the test centre to send the official score to SMU. Official Score Reports can be sent via the following Institution Code: **TOEFL: 9014 (Department Code: 82)**.
- FAQ: IELTS, UKVI (Academic) or TOEFL is required for applicants whose Degree programme (Bachelor's/Master's/PhD) was not taught in English. Minimum Requirements [IELTS/UKVI (Academic)/TOEFL]: **IELTS/UKVI (Academic) - Min 6.5**, or **TOEFL - Min 90**. SMU’s TOEFL Code: **9014**.

Program Overview.content:
18 months full-time (with flexibility to complete in 11 months); 30 months part-time (with flexibility to complete in 23 months).
The SMU Master of Sustainability (MST) programme delivers an inter-disciplinary curriculum, drawing on the breadth of domains across SMU schools to prepare students for current and future jobs in the green economy. Through the MST, students will engage in learning about the sustainable use of organisational and natural resources in service of socially equitable outcomes through an emphasis on essential core skills in sustainability reasoning, communication, coordination, and management. They would also gain familiarity with the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the fundamentals of Singapore's Green Plan 2030. Recognising the dynamic nature of sustainability roles across various sectors, the programme is led by the School of Social Sciences and College of Integrative Studies to prepare students for thriving careers in the green economy.
The programme is a first-of-its-kind programme at SMU that merges the strengths of the School of Social Sciences and College of Integrative Studies, offering an inter-disciplinary, industry-aligned curriculum. It is designed to align with major international regulatory frameworks, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs), and the Singapore Green Plan 2030. Students deepen their knowledge by selecting one of three thematic tracks in the areas of **Sustainable Resource Management**, **Urban Systems Management**, or **Environment and Sustainable Development**, or develop a broad sustainable lens without a specialisation.
Designed for flexibility, the MST programme is available in both full-time and part-time formats. It operates on 3 regular terms comprising 10 study weeks, 1 term break recess week and 1 week to administer examinations each term. All classes are held either on weekday evenings from 7pm onwards, Saturday mornings from 8.15am onwards, or Saturday afternoons from 12pm onwards. MST class sessions are 3 hours long, and are conducted in a highly interactive, seminar-styled manner. Class sessions combine lectures with discussions and group work. Through the pedagogy, students have the opportunity to interact closely with faculty, full-time professional instructors, and student teaching assistants. Students also meet with industry experts who share their experiences and perspectives through regular seminars organised by the MST programme.
The MST programme is designed to empower students as global citizens of tomorrow by providing a transformative educational experience and fostering meaningful engagement with the world around them. Students are required to complete 7 core modules, 3 courses from one of three thematic tracks, 2 MST electives, an open elective, participate in an internship or SMU-X and complete the postgraduate professional development requirement. Internship is optional for full-time students and exemptions will be made for part-time students who are currently employed. Students may also take an SMU-X course to fulfil the immersion requirement.
Industries MST graduates will work in include development finance, sustainability reporting and assurance, ESG and sustainability solution marketing, corporate strategy and development, strategic sustainability consulting, and sustainability policy professional. MST graduates will be equipped to embark on sustainability and ESG related roles including but not limited to corporate strategy and development, strategic sustainability consulting, public policy, sustainability reporting and assurance, development finance, ESG and sustainability solution marketing. All students will have a dedicated career coach assigned throughout the Masters Programme, with support including career planning and coaching, internship and job search, resume and cover letter critique, interview preparation, personality inventories, recruitment and networking events, and career development workshops. The MST programme director and manager works closely with industry partners and SMU Career Services Office to offer internship opportunities for students.

Curriculum.content:
- The Master of Sustainability (MST) is available in both full-time and part-time formats: **18 months full-time** with flexibility to complete in **11 months**, and **30 months part-time** with flexibility to complete in **23 months**. Full-time candidature is a minimum of one year and up to **5 terms**; part-time candidature is a minimum of two years to a maximum of **8 terms**.
- The programme operates on **3 regular terms** comprising **10 study weeks**, **1 term break recess week** and **1 week** to administer examinations each term. During a regular term, full-time students may take up to **5 Course Units (CUs)**, while part-time students may take up to **3 CUs**. Students may also enrol in special terms within their normal candidature period; special terms are held from July to August and November to December, with **10 sessions delivered through twice-weekly classes**.
- All classes are held either on weekday evenings from **7pm onwards**, Saturday mornings from **8.15am onwards**, or Saturday afternoons from **12pm onwards**. Full-time students may have some weekday morning or afternoon classes (**8.15am, 12pm or 3.30pm onwards**) in their first term. MST class sessions are **3 hours long** and conducted in a highly interactive, seminar-styled manner.
- Students are required to complete **7 core modules**, **3 courses from one of three thematic tracks**, **2 MST electives**, **an open elective**, participate in **an internship or SMU-X**, and complete the **postgraduate professional development requirement**.
- **Programme Core (7 CUs):** Principles of Climate Change; Collaborative Governance; UN SDG and Sustainability Policy; Inequalities in Sustainability; Systems Thinking; Sustainability Reporting; Foundations in Sustainable Finance. The seven programme core courses are compulsory and non-exemptible.
- **Thematic Track Core (3 CUs):** Sustainable Resource Management (SRM), Urban Systems Management (USM), or Environment and Sustainable Development (ESD).
- **Sustainable Resource Management (SRM):** Sustainable Agriculture & Food Systems; Energy Transitions for Sustainability; Politics of Water / Sustainable Infrastructure & Water. Politics of Water and Sustainable Infrastructure & Water are interchangeable under the Sustainable Resource Management track.
- **Urban Systems Management (USM):** Business and Climate Change; Principles of the Circular Economy; Urban Sustainability.
- **Environment and Sustainable Development (ESD):** Social Entrepreneurship & Financial Inclusion; Development, Poverty and Sustainability or Sustainability Law; Environmental Economics.
- Students may select one specialised thematic track **or** develop a broad sustainable lens without a specialisation and choose any combination of **5 electives** from the tracks or the common electives basket.
- **Common Electives (2 CUs):** Psychology of Sustainability; Behavioural Insights for Sustainability; Digital Technologies for Sustainability; Sustainability Innovation; AI and Sustainable Development; Sustainable Infrastructure & Water; Independent Study Module. The list of common electives is not exhaustive and varies termly.
- **Internship or SMU-X Course (1 CU):** Internship is optional for full-time students and exemptions will be made for part-time students who are currently employed. Students may also take an SMU-X course to fulfil the immersion requirement. Typically, the internship period is **10 weeks**; students do their internship during the one year full-time study candidature and may do their internship during term time while taking evening classes.
- **Open Elective (1 CU):** Select one course from any of the thematic tracks and common electives, or from selected Master courses offered by other SMU schools.
- **Postgraduate Professional Development (1 CU):** Select **4 workshop topics** during the candidature period. Visit [https://smu.sg/pgpd](https://smu.sg/pgpd) for more details.
- Students may read up to **2 additional CUs** beyond the graduation requirement.
- Students may switch between full-time and part-time modes of candidature at any time, but the change can only be made once and is subject to approval from the MST programme director. Students may also switch to another track after declaration, but the change can only be made once and is subject to approval from the MST programme director.

Cost of Attendance.content:
Living expenses will vary depending on your lifestyle and accommodation. However, the average international student would be able to stay within a monthly budget of S$2000 - with change to spare. Estimated breakdown of basic living expenses:
| Item | Cost Per Month |
| --- | --- |
| **Accommodation** | **S$250 - S$800** |
| **Utilities** | **S$40 - S$100** |
| **Transportation** | **S$200** |
| **Telecommunications** | **S$50** |
| **Books & Stationery** | **S$200 per term** |
| **Personal Expenses (mobile phone, meals, etc)** | **S$100 - S$300** |
| **Food** | **S$300 - S$450** |

Financial Aid.content:
All candidates are automatically submitted for consideration for MST Academic Excellence Scholarship, MST Scholarship and SMU Masters ASEAN Scholarships upon meeting the respective scholarship criteria.
- **Master of Sustainability (MST) Academic Excellence Scholarship**: Each scholarship, valued at **S$10,000**, is tenable for the duration of the scholar's studies, subject to good academic results. The Scholarship will offer partial financial support towards tuition fees. No bond is required. No application is required; it is awarded to students enrolled in the MST programme after due consideration by the faculty. Eligibility criteria include outstanding academic results; leadership potential, resourcefulness, and innovative thinking; qualities to be a good ambassador of the MST; and must not be a concurrent recipient of other scholarship or sponsorship. The recipient must maintain a cumulative minimum GPA of **3.0**.
- **Master of Sustainability (MST) Scholarship**: Each scholarship, valued at **S$5,000**, is tenable for the duration of the scholar's studies, subject to good academic results. The Scholarship will offer partial financial support towards tuition fees. No bond is required. No application is required; it is awarded to students in the MST Programme after due consideration by the faculty. Eligibility criteria include good academic results; leadership potential, resourcefulness, and innovative thinking; qualities to be a good ambassador of the MST; must not be a concurrent recipient of other scholarship or sponsorship; and special consideration may be given to students with financial needs. The recipient must maintain a cumulative minimum GPA of **3.0**.
- **SMU Masters ASEAN Scholarship**: The scholarship comprises a monetary award of **S$10,000** (inclusive of GST) that co-funds outstanding individuals in his/her pursuit of the MST. No bond is required. All eligible applicants are automatically considered; no additional application is required. Eligibility criteria include citizenship of ASEAN member countries or observer nations (Papua New Guinea and Timor-Leste); recipient must matriculate into the MST programme; candidate’s academic entry criteria is “very good” or “excellent” (**Minimum GMAT score 650 or equivalent**); leadership potential; qualities of MST ambassador; must not be a recipient of other scholarship or sponsorship; special consideration may be given to students with financial needs.
- **SMU Warriors Scholarship (SWS)**: For more details, visit [SMU Warriors Scholarship | SMU PG Admissions](https://masters.smu.edu.sg/smu-warriors-scholarship). Only MINDEF personnel who are Singapore citizens with not less than 10 years of full-time military service shall be eligible to apply. The applicant must be due to retire from MINDEF within no more than 3 years after the start of the relevant programme, or have retired from MINDEF for not more than 1 year prior to the start of the relevant programme, and in any event must be in-service at the point of application to SMU; satisfy all admission requirements imposed by the relevant postgraduate degree; and be recommended by SAF Personnel Management Centre (PMC) and Career Transition Resource Centre (CTRC).
- **Jollibee Group Foundation Postgraduate Scholarship**: Each scholarship award is valued at **S$20,000**. Each scholarship is tenable for the duration of the scholar's studies (up to two years), subject to good academic results. The Scholarship will offer financial support towards MST tuition fees. No bond is required. A separate application for the Jollibee Group Postgraduate Scholarship is required, after application to the MST programme has been completed. Valid for **2024-2026 intakes**. Successful MST applicants will be required to submit a separate application form for the scholarship [here](https://forms.office.com/r/FwS13sCwds). Eligibility criteria include full-time students successfully admitted to the MST programme; citizens of the Philippines; good academic achievements, as determined by SMU; those with demonstrated greater financial needs will be prioritised; and must not be a concurrent recipient of other scholarship or sponsorship. The recipient must maintain a cumulative minimum GPA of **3.0**.
- **Lee Kuan Yew Scholarship**: Scholarship recipients will receive full tuition fees coverage and an annual allowance of **S$50,000** for up to 2 years if they are pursuing a Master’s degree. Public sector awardees who are already sponsored by their agencies for their postgraduate studies will receive a one-off sum of **S$10,000**. Eligibility criteria: Singapore citizen with at least a Second Upper Honours Degree or equivalent Degree; excellent track record of leadership and service within or beyond applicant's profession. More information and application form/procedures are available [here](https://www.psc.gov.sg/home).
- **Sustainability Stewardship Award for the Top Master of Sustainability Student**: Prize value of **S$3,000**. One Award will be awarded in each academic year. Candidates must be matriculated Master of Sustainability students in their final year of study. The Award will be awarded to the top student who has achieved exceptional academic results and demonstrated commitment in the sustainability industry. Eligible candidates would be invited to respond to questions pertaining to their area of study and future endeavours in sustainability, which will be vetted by the review committee.

Attractive discounts are available to eligible students including SMU Alumni, Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents, MINDEF/SAFTI staff, ASEAN Nationals and other groups. Please visit [HERE](http://publiceservices.smu.edu.sg/psc/ps/EMPLOYEE/HRMS/c/SA_LEARNER_SERVICES.SIS_SF_TUT_DS_CALC.GBL) for details. Where a student qualifies for more than one discount, only the higher discount amount will be applicable.
Scholarships are available for deserving students.
SkillsFuture funding for Singapore Citizens:
1. Singaporeans aged 25 and above can use their SkillsFuture Credit to offset the tuition fees. [Click on this link for more details.](https://www.skillsfuture.gov.sg/initiatives/early-career/credit)
2. The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme offers Singaporeans aged 40 years and above the opportunity to receive the SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) Top-up of **S$4,000**. This credit is intended to help offset out-of-pocket tuition fees, starting from the Academic Year 2024/2025 intake, commencing on or after **1 May 2024**. Please visit [https://www.skillsfuture.gov.sg/level-up-programme](https://www.skillsfuture.gov.sg/level-up-programme) for further details.
Singapore Citizens with eligible Post Secondary Education Account (PSEA) may utilize balance funds for tuition fees. [Click on this link for more details.](https://www.moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/psea)
FAQ: Selected scholarships are available. For more details on scholarships, please refer to this page: [Scholarships](https://masters.smu.edu.sg/programme/master-of-sustainability#admissions-tab). Singaporeans aged 25 and above can use their SkillsFuture Credit from the Government to pay for a wide range of approved skills-related courses.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
I’ve received an offer, but would like to defer my admission to the next intake. Is this possible? Deferment is possible but you will have to pay the **$5,000 acceptance fee** in order to secure your place. Otherwise the offer will lapse and you will have to re-apply and be re-considered.
For the SMU Masters ASEAN Scholarship: Recipient must matriculate into the MST programme to receive the award. Deferment of studies beyond SMU’s financial year would void the scholarship award.
